question: The SI unit of temperature is/are _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __Kelvin__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Kelvin__ is the SI unit of temperature.
 
• The Kelvin scale starts at absolute zero, where all thermal motion ceases.
 
• It is used in scientific measurements because it is an absolute scale.
 
• One Kelvin is equivalent to one degree Celsius in terms of size.
 
• However, the Kelvin scale does not use negative numbers, as it starts at absolute zero.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Fahrenheit:**

 
 
• A temperature scale where water freezes at 32°F and boils at 212°F.
 
• It is not a part of the SI system.
 
 
 
• **Celsius:**
 
 
• The Celsius scale is commonly used for everyday temperature measurements.
 
• However, it is not the official SI unit of temperature.
